title: The logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The course is an exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) of the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality for convex bodies that are symmetric about the origin: the Wulff body of the geometric mean of two support functions has volume at least the geometric mean of the volumes. The first lesson proves the facts about support functions and Wulff bodies that are needed, and proves that the inequality in dimension n follows from a variance bound for explicit smooth probability densities (soft polytopes), by a second derivative of the logarithm of an integral and three limits; it also derives the additive inequality for powers between 0 and 1. The second lesson defines moment pairs (a density Z^-1 e^-V as the image of e^-phi under the gradient of phi), states as the named hypothesis (M) the existence of an even moment potential with Hessian at most 4/eps, and proves, for every moment pair, the adjoint identities, the properties of the operator A f = x . grad f - tau : D^2 f, and the identities for the test fields B, W and u = A(A-1)f, including the Hessian identity. The third lesson proves the tensor estimate for every moment pair: E u^2 >= E tr(M B H B) + E W^T H W, where H is the Hessian of V; the difference of E tr((D_x W)^2) and E tr(M B H B) is written as the mean of three squares. The fourth lesson proves, for an even moment pair with bounded Hessian tau and under the named hypothesis (ER) of interior elliptic regularity, that the functions A(A-1)f with f even and compactly supported are dense in the even functions of L^2(mu) with mean zero. The fifth lesson proves the variance bound from the tensor estimate and the density theorem by two Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities for each summand, and with it the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality in every dimension, under the two named hypotheses (M) and (ER); for the exponent q = 2 it proves the variance bound without any hypothesis, by the theorem on entrywise products of positive semidefinite matrices. So the course contains the whole argument of the manuscript for its main theorem except the proofs of two statements from the literature: the existence of moment coordinates with a bounded Hessian, and interior regularity for an elliptic operator of order four.
prerequisites: the Lebesgue integral in R^n with the theorems of dominated and monotone convergence (core course Measure and Integration)
compact convex sets in R^n and Hoelder's inequality for finite sums; the lesson proves the facts about support functions that it uses

checks.reading: The manuscript 'The logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski conjecture' (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026) was read in full on 12 Oct 2026 (eight sections of TeX); a first-pass check of its steps, with three check programs, is recorded in plan/OPENAI_091_SCOPING_20261012.md. Lesson 1 was written against Sections 1, 2 and 8.1. Every step was derived: the support-function facts (the manuscript uses them without proof; the lesson proves them, including the description of a convex body by its supporting half-spaces through a nearest point); the formula (log Z)'' = Var - E V''; the limits q to infinity (dominated convergence), eps to 0 (monotone convergence) and finitely many directions to all directions (continuity from above); dimension one; the corollary for 0 < p < 1. Example 2.1 (boxes with the same axes: the Wulff body is the box of the geometric means, with equality) and the four exercises are additions; their statements were verified by hand, Exercise 7.2 also numerically (plan/checks_20261012/lb_check_variance.py: E y^q = Var y^q = 1/q for q = 2, 4, 6, 10). No discrepancy with the manuscript. Lesson 2 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 3 (statement of the lemma on moment coordinates only) and Section 4. The lemma on moment coordinates is not proved in the course: it is the named hypothesis (M), with the origin of its proof relayed from the manuscript. The lesson separates what holds for every moment pair (Sections 2 to 4 of the lesson; neither evenness nor the bound for the Hessian is used there) and derives the moment equation from the push-forward property (Lemma 1.1), which the manuscript lists as part of the statement. Every identity of Section 4 was derived by hand: the adjoint of d/dz_k; the row adjoint identity and delta_mu tau = x; the formula, the symmetry and the product rule for A; W = delta_mu B; the pairing; W = tau grad_x (Af - f) with all terms; the Hessian identity. Checked numerically (plan/checks_20261012/lb_check_tensor.py, an explicit moment pair on R^2 that is neither even nor separable): D_z W symmetric (8e-15), W = grad_z (Af - f) (4e-15), the pairing (54.10874205 in all three forms), the Hessian identity (6.71412576 on both sides). Example 1.2, Example 4.2 and the exercises are additions and were computed by hand. No discrepancy with the manuscript. Lesson 3 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 6 (the lemma 'Moment-coordinate tensor estimate'). Every step was derived by hand: the Bochner identity; the first and second derivative of the moment equation; D_z W = B + R with R symmetric; the trace expansion; the H expansion; the three contractions; the norm of Sym J; the sum of squares. Difference of presentation: the manuscript evaluates the three contractions after a constant linear change of coordinates that makes tau the identity at a point and argues by invariance; the lesson defines the normalized tensors S-hat and J-hat with the square roots of tau and verifies the three identities by direct contraction in arbitrary coordinates. Checked numerically (plan/checks_20261012/lb_check_tensor.py and lb_check_tensor2.py; an explicit moment pair on R^2 that is neither even nor separable, 601 x 601 grid): the Bochner identity (375.79253284 on both sides); the twice-differentiated moment equation pointwise (1e-14); both expansions (8 digits); the three contractions pointwise against 2|S-hat|^2 + 2<S-hat,J-hat>, 2<S-hat,J-hat> + <J-hat,J-hat^(12)> and |J-hat|^2 (1e-13); the final identity 350.40149521 = 281.14597983 + 69.25551538. Example 6.2 and the exercises were computed by hand. No error found in Section 6 of the manuscript. Lesson 4 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 5 (the lemma 'Density of even tests'). Every step was derived by hand: the weak equation P g = 0 for a function orthogonal to the tests (even and odd parts; the principal symbol rho (xi . tau xi)^2); the constants B and K of the cutoffs; the expansion of (A-1)(eta^4 g); the two inequalities X <= aG + 8BY/r and Y^2 <= GX + 2BGY/r with a = 1 + 4K + 12B^2; the harmonic part (constant); the eigenvalue-one part (linear, by the Hessian identity applied to eta_r v); the conclusion. The interior regularity theorem for an elliptic operator of order 4, which the manuscript cites from lecture notes, is the named hypothesis (ER) of the lesson. The lesson states explicitly the bounds Y <= (10B + sqrt a) G and X <= (a + 8B(10B + sqrt a)) G. A first version of the solution of Exercise 6.1 called P x^4 a multiple of a Hermite polynomial; it is 12 H_4 + 12 H_2, and the solution was corrected before staging. No error found in Section 5 of the manuscript. Lesson 5 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 7 (proof of the variance bound) and Section 8 (consequences). Every step was derived by hand: the homogeneity relations; m_i = q a_i with the cutoff argument; d_i = E tr(B H_i); the first Cauchy-Schwarz inequality with the matrices H_i^(1/2) tau^(1/2) and H_i^(1/2) B M^(1/2); the second with the form E X^T H_i Y; the sum q d_i^2 / m_i = d_i^2 / a_i; the passage to all even centered u by density; the final duality step. Proposition 6.1 (the case q = 2 by the Schur product theorem) is an addition: it gives an unconditional proof of the variance bound for Gaussian soft polytopes. Exercise 7.4 was replaced before staging: a first version mixed two different potentials; the present one (V = psi = x^2 in dimension 1) was computed through, and all its inequalities are equalities. The variance bound itself was tested by quadrature (plan/checks_20261012/lb_check_variance.py): 119 converged instances in dimension 2 and 74 in dimension 3 with q in {2, 4, 6, 8}; it holds in all of them. No error found in Section 7 of the manuscript. Section 8.2 (even log-concave measures) is relayed and not in the course.

open_obligations: Not in the course: the corollary of Section 8.2 of the manuscript for even log-concave measures and the (B)-property for scalar dilations; it uses a transfer theorem of Saroglou and a theorem of Borell. The main theorem (the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality) and the corollary for 0 < p < 1 are in the course, proved from the named hypotheses (M) and (ER).

Named hypothesis (M) of the second lesson: for n >= 2, eps > 0 and a smooth even V with D^2 V >= eps, there is an even smooth phi such that (V, phi) is a moment pair and D^2 phi <= 4/eps. This is the lemma on moment coordinates of the manuscript (Section 3). It is not proved in the course and was not checked beyond reading; according to the manuscript its proof uses the moment theorem of Berman and Berndtsson for a density on a ball, Klartag's bound for the Hessian of the moment potential, and interior estimates for elliptic equations (Evans-Krylov, Schauder). The programme has none of these. The density argument of the manuscript (Section 5) also uses interior regularity for a fourth-order elliptic operator; whether the programme has an exact provider is still to be settled.
Relayed and not checked: the statements about the history of the conjecture (attributed to the manuscript in the first lesson).

Named hypothesis (ER) of the fourth lesson: interior regularity for an elliptic operator of order 4 with smooth coefficients (a locally square-integrable function annihilated by the transposed operator in the sense of distributions is smooth). It is not proved in the course. The programme has courses on elliptic operators (AN-01 to AN-05, elliptic-operators-and-boundary-problems); an exact provider of this statement has not been located yet.
